business: GradTrail, a free, open-source, self-hosted job-search and application workspace
why_not: I would not set this up right now. I already have a spreadsheet, and Docker plus source keys sounds like more work than it saves unless I can see a useful search working quickly.
The filters and original links would save me time, but I would probably keep checking the boards I already know instead of setting up Docker on my limited laptop.

The filters and original links sound useful for finding internships, but I need to know whether the posting dates and eligibility details stay current before I trust it with my search. Docker setup also feels like a lot when I could keep checking the boards directly.
why_yes: Keeping my application history on my own machine is appealing, and the features cover the scattered tracking I do now. I would try it once, but Docker setup could make me quit before I get to the useful parts.

I would try it because it is free and I like keeping my application data on my own computer; the Hacker News startup posts could surface roles outside the usual boards. I would still rely on alumni and developer communities for referrals, and I might give up if Docker setup takes too long.

I would try a free tool that brings internship listings and application follow-ups together, and the project based application-material help sounds useful. I would only install it when I have time to deal with Docker, and I would skip optional AI if the provider cost is unclear.
